title: Polymarket saw $600 million in election trades after the elections were over
gist: WIRED reports that two Polymarket election markets (Ethiopia and Romania) drew over $600 million in volume, with about $284 million of the Ethiopian volume coming from account pairs trading with each other. Experts see wash trading or activity farming for a possible Polymarket token airdrop, while the company is valued at about $21 billion.

insights.claim: Two global election markets on Polymarket's offshore platform generated over $600 million in volume, mostly on long-shot candidates who did not win.
insights.speaker: WIRED
insights.so_what: Headline volume may overstate genuine interest and trading activity.

insights.claim: In the Ethiopia market just $173,000 was wagered on winner Abiy Ahmed versus over $41 million on chief of staff Shimelis Abdisa, with total volume above $285 million nearly all on losing candidates.
insights.speaker: WIRED
insights.so_what: Volume contradicting odds is a red flag for manipulation.

insights.claim: About $284 million of the Ethiopian volume came from pairs of accounts repeatedly buying and selling with each other, according to former Polymarket trader Chris Park of MSR Decode.
insights.speaker: WIRED
insights.so_what: Indicates most volume was circular rather than economic.
insights.quote: “Nearly all of it—about $284 million—came from pairs of accounts repeatedly buying and selling with each other,”

insights.claim: In the Romania market, a flagging algorithm by Rajiv Sethi's team identified 99.6 percent of volume in certain weeks as wash trading after Polymarket kept the original market open alongside the rerun election.
insights.speaker: WIRED
insights.so_what: Shows manipulation persisted in 'zombie' markets left open.
insights.quote: “99.6 percent of volume in this market for certain weeks has been wash trading,”
insights.locator: Another market about a 2024 election in Romania

insights.claim: Polymarket's rules kept the Ethiopia market open until the prime minister was sworn in, so it traded for 123 days after the election result was a foregone conclusion, a phenomenon Sethi calls a 'zombie market'.
insights.speaker: WIRED
insights.so_what: Market design and resolution rules create room for pointless or manipulative trading.
insights.locator: The timing of these trades made things even weirder

insights.claim: Polymarket's head of investigations says the team flagged the activity and blocked the accounts, but the company did not explain why such volume traded before action was taken.
insights.speaker: WIRED
insights.so_what: Surveillance latency is an open risk for the platform.

themes.theme: Activity farming and the token incentive

insights.claim: MSR Decode's most likely explanation is 'activity farming' to inflate volume, because traders may have expected benefits if Polymarket launched a token, after its chief marketing officer said in 2025 there 'would be a token'.
insights.speaker: WIRED
insights.so_what: Token expectations can drive artificial volume, so treat volume metrics with caution.

insights.claim: MSR Decode analyzed over 38,000 post-election trade loops, found over 98 percent left neither side gaining or losing, and a median hold time of nine seconds, arguing against profit-seeking algorithmic trading.
insights.speaker: WIRED
insights.so_what: Quantifies the non-economic nature of the trading.
insights.locator: When MSR Decode analyzed the Ethiopian election market

insights.claim: Ulm University's Andre Guettler calls the behavior textbook examples of how participants farm a potential airdrop, a pattern previously seen in crypto.
insights.speaker: WIRED
insights.so_what: Parallels crypto airdrop farming and suggests incentive design drives fake volume.
insights.quote: “These are textbook examples on how market participants farm a potential airdrop,”
insights.locator: This type of behavior has been observed before

insights.claim: Sethi cautions that what appears to be wash trading is not always wash trading, since traders' identities are unknown.
insights.speaker: WIRED
insights.quote: “What appears to be wash trading isn’t always wash trading,”
insights.locator: Wash trading could explain what happened

insights.claim: Polymarket recently raised over $1 billion led by 1789 Capital, where Donald Trump Jr. is a partner, at about a $21 billion valuation, and announced annualized revenue above $1 billion; its growth is often measured by volume, which wash trading could inflate.
insights.speaker: WIRED
insights.so_what: Valuation narratives may rely on questionable volume metrics.

insights.claim: Kalshi denied wash trading allegations on its crypto perpetual futures market, and Sethi agrees, attributing volume to market-maker incentives.
insights.speaker: WIRED
insights.so_what: Both leading prediction markets face scrutiny; incentive programs can produce odd volume.
insights.locator: Both Polymarket and its chief rival

insights.claim: The CFTC declined to comment on whether it is examining these trades; its past Polymarket probes mostly involved insider trading, and a former CFTC employee says it would want to know about weird activity in a very large market.
insights.speaker: WIRED
insights.so_what: Regulatory risk exists since wash trading is banned on US regulated exchanges.
insights.quote: “It seems to me that the CFTC would want to know about weird activity in a very large market,”
